title: Geometrical Optics
seo_title: Grade 11 Physical Sciences: Geometrical Optics Worksheets (CAPS)
standard_text: Refraction and the refractive index, n = c/v; Snell's law, n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂; the critical angle and total internal reflection; uses of total internal reflection such as optical fibres and endoscopes. (summary of CAPS Physical Sciences, Grade 11, Physics: Geometrical optics)
meta_desc: Free Grade 11 Physical Sciences worksheets (CAPS): refraction, refractive index, Snell's law, the critical angle and total internal reflection. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂
key_sub: Light bends towards the normal when it slows down.
body_html:
How to think about it

Refraction is the change in direction of light as it passes from one medium to another, because its speed changes. The refractive index of a medium is n = c/v; a larger n means light travels more slowly. Angles are measured from the normal.

When light goes from a denser to a less dense medium, it bends away from the normal. At the critical angle the refracted angle is 90°; for larger angles all the light is reflected back (total internal reflection). This is used in optical fibres for telecommunications and endoscopes in medicine.

Example

Light slows from 3 × 10⁸ to 2 × 10⁸ m·s⁻¹ in glass. n?

n = c/v

Answer: 1,5

Example

When can total internal reflection happen?

Think about which medium the light starts in.

Answer: when light goes from a denser to a less dense medium at an angle bigger than the critical angle

Common mistakes

  • Measuring angles from the surface instead of the normal.
  • Thinking total internal reflection can happen going into glass.
  • Thinking light speeds up in water.

faq.q: Why does a straw look bent in a glass of water?
faq.a: Light from the straw refracts at the water surface, so it seems to come from a different place.
Diamond has a very high refractive index and a small critical angle, so light is totally internally reflected many times.

items.q: Ravi notices: “A hot road looks wet in the distance on a summer day.” What explains this?
c: Light bends as it passes through hot and cooler layers of air.
Light reflects off a mirror at the same angle.
items.e: This is refraction: light changes speed and direction when it enters a new material.

items.q: Light travels at 2,00 × 10<sup>8</sup> m·s⁻¹ in a material. What is its refractive index? (c = 3,0 × 10⁸ m·s⁻¹)
A ray of light enters a block from air with an angle of incidence of 70° and an angle of refraction of 38°. What is the refractive index?
items.e: n = sin i ÷ sin r = sin 70° ÷ sin 38° = 1,53.

items.q: A ray enters glass (refractive index 1,5) from air and is refracted at 15° to the normal. What was the angle of incidence?
items.e: sin i = n × sin r = 1,5 × sin 15°, so i = 22,8°.

items.q: A ray of light enters a glass block along the normal. What happens to the light?
c: It slows down but does not bend.
It slows down and bends away from the normal.
It speeds up and bends away from the normal.
It speeds up and bends towards the normal.
items.e: Light changes speed when it enters a different medium, so it bends (refracts) unless it travels along the normal.

items.e: n = sin i ÷ sin r = sin 50° ÷ sin 35° = 1,34.
